channel.title: Information Hub — Daily Intelligence Library
channel.description: Deep, structured briefings written daily by an autonomous multi-provider AI pipeline.

item.title: US interest rates raised for first time in three years
item.description: The Federal Reserve raised rates to 3.75%-4% amid persistent inflation, despite President Trump's calls for cuts. The move signals a commitment to price stability, though political tension and market impacts remain.

item.title: Snapchat 'willing to implement' daily time limits for teens, boss tells BBC
item.description: Snapchat CEO Evan Spiegel says the firm is open to imposing daily usage caps for teenage users, echoing Meta’s recent settlement, while unveiling new AI‑powered Specs glasses.

item.title: Photos show widespread damage at US sites from Iranian attacks
item.description: Satellite‑style images obtained by CBS News reveal extensive destruction of US military installations across Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, including a crippled Boeing E‑3 Sentry and flattened bases. The disclosures follow a Pentagon watchdog report confirming hundreds of damaged structures and a $3.7 bn equipment loss, raising questions about US defensive preparedness and the broader strategic impact o

item.title: Burnham rejects 'tax and spend socialist' comments
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has defended his economic approach after former Bank of England chief economist Andy Haldane warned that markets view his government as a “traditional tax and spend socialist” administration. Burnham stressed that difficult fiscal decisions are already being taken, despite rising borrowing costs and pressure from unions to fund energy subsidies.

item.title: Call to raise tax thresholds among union demands ahead of Budget
item.description: Unions that donate to Labour are meeting Chancellor John Healey to press demands such as unfreezing tax thresholds, reversing winter‑fuel cuts, taxing big tech, and advancing North Sea oil projects. The push aims to restore fairness for lower‑paid workers and signal a new fiscal direction for the government.

item.title: Weave Router 2.0 – Subscription Aware Coding Agent Router
item.description: Weave Router 2.0 introduces a subscription‑aware coding agent that dynamically routes development tasks to the most suitable AI models, promising faster build cycles and granular billing for developers worldwide.

item.title: Gemini 3.8 & 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
item.description: Google’s Gemini 3.8 audio models push the frontier of real‑time, multimodal interaction, adding a live‑extended thinking mode that lets LLMs retain context across spoken turns. The launch intensifies the agentic AI race with OpenAI and Anthropic, while raising fresh questions about regulation, open‑source access, and emerging markets such as Myanmar.

item.title: Assad regime planned US journalist's kidnap for weeks, BBC finds
item.description: BBC investigative reporting reveals that the abduction of US journalist Austin Tice in 2012 was a pre‑meditated operation approved by President Bashar al‑Assad, contradicting earlier assumptions of a chance kidnapping. The case underscores the Syrian regime’s willingness to target foreign reporters and raises fresh questions about US‑Syria diplomatic leverage.

item.title: All support acts on Ed Sheeran's US tour quit after Macklemore dropped
item.description: Ed Sheeran's US tour support acts, including Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Beoga, have withdrawn after Macklemore was removed for pro‑Palestinian remarks, highlighting tensions between artistic expression, venue politics and audience expectations.

item.title: Denmark says Russian warship fired flares at military helicopter
item.description: A Danish Fennec helicopter was targeted by emergency flares from a Russian frigate in the Baltic Sea, prompting diplomatic summons and heightened NATO vigilance after a separate drone was shot down over Lithuania.

item.title: What weapon could the US have put into space?
item.description: The United States has announced an on‑orbit weapon to protect its assets, sparking speculation about its nature and intensifying a nascent arms race in space. Analysts consider electronic‑warfare platforms, kinetic kill vehicles, and grappling satellites as possibilities, while China, Russia and other powers already possess anti‑satellite capabilities and are expanding their own programmes.

item.title: UK in talks about joining global defence bank led by Canada
item.description: The UK is in preliminary talks to join Canada‑led Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB), which promises cheaper loans for defence projects. Chancellor John Healey is weighing the move after his predecessor rejected it, while the government signals a commitment to boost defence industrial capacity. The discussions coincide with heightened NATO activity and a broader push to increase UK defen

item.title: Dan Thomas resigns as Reform Wales leader after arrest on suspicion of assault
item.description: Reform Wales leader Dan Thomas stepped down following a Gwent Police arrest over alleged assault and coercive behaviour, though he was released without charge. The resignation coincides with a defection of another Reform MS and raises questions about the party’s internal stability ahead of the next Senedd election.

item.title: Buddy AI Access (MCP)
item.description: Buddy AI Access (MCP) gives agents more than just code repos by providing a unified, protocol‑driven interface to external data, powered by major LLMs and open‑source tooling to accelerate AI‑driven workflows.

item.title: Axari – Delegating Security Busywork to an AI Twin
item.description: Axari introduces an agentic AI assistant that automates routine security tasks, freeing security teams to focus on strategy. Built on LLM technology and offering an open‑source SDK, it raises fresh questions about regulation, data governance, and the future of AI‑augmented security operations.

item.title: US limits visas for South African officials over alleged anti‑white discrimination
item.description: The United States has imposed visa restrictions on South African officials it accuses of promoting anti‑white policies, marking a sharp escalation in bilateral tensions. Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned that further measures could follow if Washington’s concerns about racial discrimination are not addressed.

item.title: Trump says AI safety fears a 'hoax' as he rejects calls for greater safeguards
item.description: President Trump dismissed AI safety concerns as a hoax, likening them to the 'Global Warming Scam' and 'Russia hoax', while tech leaders and lawmakers debate mandatory kill switches and regulation.

item.title: China criticises idea it is in 'malicious competition' over AI
item.description: Beijing rebukes what it calls "threat narratives" and "malicious competition" in AI, responding to US calls for a slowdown that would keep China from pulling ahead. The spat underscores the deepening rivalry between the world's two largest AI powers and the difficulty of forging a common governance framework.

item.title: AI regulation faces political deadlock as calls grow for Congress to act
item.description: President Donald Trump dismisses the need for AI guardrails, while senior Democrats and leading AI firms push for safety legislation, leaving Congress gridlocked amid election‑year pressures and procedural hurdles.

item.title: OpenAI buys smartphone camera maker Glass Imaging for $300 million, report says
item.description: OpenAI has acquired smartphone camera specialist Glass Imaging for over $300 million, bringing together Apple‑originated portrait expertise and advanced AI‑driven computational photography. The deal underscores OpenAI’s push into consumer hardware and signals a shift toward on‑device AI optimization, potentially influencing future ChatGPT‑powered imaging experiences.

item.title: Jensen Huang took a call from Trump, and showed off something else, too
item.description: President Trump live‑called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on stage at the All‑In conference, using a Samsung Galaxy Fold 8, and discussed AI safety while dismissing concerns as a "hoax." The episode highlights Nvidia’s deep ties to AI demand, the intensifying policy debate over AI regulation, and how high‑profile political moments are leveraged for product visibility.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang tells Trump ‘we’re not going to let [an AI slowdown] happen’
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly pledged to President Trump that the company will not allow an AI development slowdown, countering calls from Anthropic, Elon Musk, and Sam Altman to pause progress. The exchange highlighted growing tension between rapid AI expansion, environmental concerns over data centers, and geopolitical competition, with Trump framing the slowdown push as a potential psyop.

item.title: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station
item.description: A Russian drone struck a stationary Ukrainian locomotive near the Polish border minutes after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and senior European security officials had departed the same line. No casualties were reported, but the attack underscores Russia’s escalating campaign against critical rail infrastructure and raises the stakes for NATO and EU security.

item.title: Trump downplays warnings of AI risks, citing rivalry with China
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump dismissed recent expert warnings about AI dangers, framing the debate as a strategic competition with China and insisting the United States must retain its lead. Meanwhile, top AI executives and researchers are calling for a coordinated slowdown, highlighting fears that unchecked development could threaten humanity.

item.title: Questions mount over what an AI 'slowdown' would look like
item.description: Top AI executives and researchers are calling for a pause in development, yet the practical meaning, enforcement, and impact of such a slowdown remain unclear, raising doubts about whether the industry can self‑regulate or if geopolitical and economic forces will dictate the pace of progress.

item.title: Insight Partners’ Deven Parekh on why the firm is diversifying while everyone else bets the farm on OpenAI and Anthropic
item.description: Deven Parekh explains Insight Partners’ deliberate diversification in AI, despite the sector’s concentration on OpenAI and Anthropic, citing balanced risk, stage‑dependent investing, and a focus on portfolio performance over headline‑grabbing bets.

item.title: Reform confident it won't need to repay any of £72m under proposed new donor rules
item.description: Reform UK insists its £72m haul from crypto billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne is legal under both current and forthcoming rules, even as the government moves to cap overseas donations retrospectively. Housing Secretary Angela Rayner warns non‑compliant donors may have to return funds, fuelling a broader debate over mega‑donors and democratic integrity.

item.title: Will record donations to Reform go down as a moment of political change?
item.description: Reform UK received two record‑breaking £36m donations, swelling its war chest to £72m and reigniting debate over party financing. Prime Minister Andy Burnham faces mounting pressure to tighten donation rules, including caps on overseas Britons and crypto donors, while Downing Street insists the cash influx will not accelerate an early election. The surge could reshape campaign logistics and force

item.title: Neopress – AI‑Driven Conversational Website Builder
item.description: Neopress lets users create and grow websites through a chat‑based interface powered by large language models. By blending agentic AI, low‑code design, and real‑time analytics, it aims to democratise web development while raising questions about data governance, open‑source alternatives, and regulatory oversight.

item.title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has published an essay urging a coordinated slowdown in AI model development, citing serious existential risks and calling for independent monitoring, industry‑wide and global regulation. The appeal has gained support from rival executives Sam Altman and Elon Musk, while insiders warn that current progress could endanger humanity within years.

item.title: Trump's comments on a united Ireland may have targeted audience across the Atlantic
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump suggested a future unified Ireland during a visit to the island, sparking debate over whether this reflects a new policy or a personal remark. Analysts note the timing coincides with tight midterm elections and a broader push for Irish‑American votes, while senior officials reaffirm continued U.S. support for the Good Friday Agreement.

item.title: Fire at nursing home in Chile kills 16 residents
item.description: A devastating blaze at El Edén nursing home in Chile’s Araucanía region claimed at least 16 elderly lives and prompted a nationwide review of care facilities. President José Antonio Kast has ordered an inquiry, highlighting systemic safety gaps and spurring debate over the role of AI‑driven monitoring technologies in preventing such tragedies.

item.title: Anthropic CEO Outlines Plan to Pace the Frontier
item.description: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei proposes three broad strategies to slow AI development, including third‑party embedded evaluators, coordinated safety standards among democratic AI firms, and limited global coordination with China, while OpenAI and Elon Musk signal support for the “pacing” concept.

item.title: OpenAI’s Sam Altman says it would be ‘ill‑advised’ to go public in 2026
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has confirmed the company will not pursue an IPO in 2026, citing safety concerns and volatile market conditions, pushing any public offering to 2027 or later. The delay reflects broader industry caution around AI governance and recent security incidents, while giving OpenAI more flexibility to focus on product development and research. Analysts see the move as a strategic eff

item.title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record
item.description: Reform UK has secured £72 million in record‑breaking donations from cryptocurrency investors Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo, dwarfing the total raised by all UK parties last year and prompting fresh calls for donation caps. The influx of cash has placed the party on an election footing, while intensifying scrutiny over foreign funding and parliamentary standards.

item.title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying
item.description: The House of Commons rejected the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill by 286‑270, halting the latest push to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales. The defeat reflects deep divisions over safeguards, palliative care funding and the role of doctors in end‑of‑life decisions.

item.title: They lost their jobs after posting about Charlie Kirk, but some have no regrets
item.description: Hundreds of Americans were dismissed or disciplined after posting critical remarks about the slain conservative activist Charlie Kirk. While a few have secured multi‑million settlements, most, like sports writer Gerald Bourguet, are rebuilding their lives amid a broader debate over free speech, corporate policy, and AI‑driven content moderation.

item.title: AI staff 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future, ex-Anthropic researcher tells BBC
item.description: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon says AI engineers are terrified that rapid progress could lead to an existential crisis within years. The warning adds weight to recent calls from Dario Amodei, Sam Altman and Elon Musk for a coordinated global slowdown and stronger regulation.

item.title: Houthis claim major advance in Yemen and tighten grip on Red Sea shipping lane
item.description: The Iran‑backed Houthis have seized the strategic Perim Island at the Bab al‑Mandab Strait, consolidating control over a vital maritime corridor. The rapid advance has prompted Saudi Arabia to seek US military support, while the United Nations warns of a deepening humanitarian crisis.

item.title: Tragic death of woman who testified against father in notorious mafia murder of mother
item.description: Denise Cosco, who testified against her father in the brutal 2009 murder of her mother Lea Garofalo—a high‑profile Ndrangheta killing—died by suicide at age 35, echoing her mother’s fate. Her death has reignited debate over the adequacy of Italy’s witness‑protection programmes and the psychological toll on families battling organised crime. Anti‑mafia groups warn that the tragedy underscores the n

item.title: Passenger train derails in France leaving at least 44 injured
item.description: A passenger train traveling between Rouen and Caen in Normandy derailed on Friday evening, injuring 44 people including a critically injured 18-year-old woman. Emergency services deployed 140 firefighters and activated a mass‑casualty response, while SNCF reported significant service disruptions.

item.title: OpenAI’s feud with mathematicians is only escalating
item.description: Twenty‑five Fields Medalists warn that AI labs, especially OpenAI, are rushing to claim breakthroughs without proper attribution, jeopardizing academic integrity and the open‑source research culture. The dispute highlights growing tensions between rapid AI‑driven discovery and the traditional scholarly process.

item.title: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan wants US open-weight AI labs to ‘distill’ frontier models, too
item.description: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan argues that U.S. open‑weight AI labs should be allowed to distill frontier models, mirroring practices currently attributed to Chinese labs, to create a more robust, non‑Chinese open‑source AI ecosystem while avoiding regulatory overreach.

item.title: Mecka AI nears $500M valuation in Sequoia-led deal amid rush for robot training data
item.description: Mecka AI, a two‑year‑old startup that captures human motion for robot training, is close to a $500 million Sequoia‑led funding round just months after a $60 million raise. The deal underscores a fast‑growing market for real‑world, egocentric data as humanoid robotics race toward general‑purpose capabilities.

item.title: Saudi Arabia shuts key oil pipeline after drone attack launched from Iraq
item.description: Saudi Arabia closed its 1,200‑km East‑West crude pipeline after drones launched from Iraq caused damage and injuries. Iraq removed a senior commander, opened an investigation, and the incident raises fresh geopolitical risk for global oil markets.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis reportedly seize strategic Red Sea port of Mokha
item.description: Iran‑backed Houthi forces have taken control of the Red Sea city of Mokha, positioning them just 75 km from the Bab al‑Mandab Strait. The capture has displaced hundreds, intensified the Yemen war, and contributed to rising oil prices as the Houthis expand their maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Can Trump really pay $5,000 to every American adult?
item.description: President Donald Trump pledged $5,000 to each U.S. adult if Republicans win the midterms, sparking debate over legality, financing, and electoral tactics. Analysts question whether tariff revenue or executive authority could fund the $1.3 trillion outlay, calling the promise both politically risky and fiscally unsustainable.

item.title: Pilot warned Amazon cargo plane going too fast before deadly crash, data shows
item.description: Flight data from the NTSB reveals that a pilot repeatedly warned about the Amazon cargo jet’s excessive speed before it overshot the runway in Miami, leading to a fatal crash that killed five ground crew members. Inconsistent cockpit communication, late flap deployment, and multiple automated safety alerts compounded the mishap, prompting scrutiny of pilot training and airline safety protocols.

item.title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%
item.description: Labour metro mayors across ten English city regions have pledged to limit a new visitor overnight levy to a maximum of 5%, seeking a balance between local investment and concerns over cost impacts on families and the hospitality sector.

item.title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless
item.description: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch defended a proposed £4bn cut to housing benefits to fund a rise in defence spending, insisting existing tenants would be protected while suggesting some would need to move to cheaper areas.
